findings.title: Public findMany() method removed, breaking existing callers
findings.body: The refactor deletes the class's `findMany()` method, which was the main query entry point that took Prisma `BookingTimeStatusDenormalizedFindManyArgs` and returned bookings. It is replaced only by `getBaseConditions()`, which returns a raw `Prisma.Sql` fragment. Any existing code that constructs `InsightsBookingService` and calls `service.findMany({ select, where, ... })` will now fail to compile or throw at runtime. The PR contains no changes to callers, so unless all call sites were already migrated in a prior PR, this is a breaking API change. The PR description also does not mention any caller migration.

findings.title: Passing JS arrays to `= ANY(...)` may fail depending on Prisma driver serialization
findings.body: In `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` (line 164/168) and `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` (line 201), plain JavaScript arrays are interpolated into `Prisma.sql` and used as `"teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})`. Depending on the Prisma engine/driver version, raw query parameters that are JS arrays are not always serialized as PostgreSQL array types, which can produce errors like "op ANY/ALL (array) requires array on right side" or unexpected type coercion for the `teamIds` (int) case. The idiomatic safe form is `${Prisma.join(teamIds)}` inside the parentheses or an explicit `::int[]` cast. Since the author explicitly states the integration tests were never run ("I encountered test runner configuration issues"), this serialization risk is unverified and the query construction should be confirmed to actually execute against a real database before merging.

findings.title: Integration tests were never executed; author flags manual verification as required
findings.body: The PR description states the test runner had configuration issues during development and asks a human to "Run integration tests manually" because the author could not verify them. The entire PR's purpose is to make these tests pass against the new raw-SQL implementation, yet there is no evidence they were run. Merging unexecuted tests for authorization-critical SQL (org/team scoping, owner/admin checks) risks shipping broken queries that either fail at runtime or, worse, produce conditions that leak or wrongly restrict data. The tests must be executed and passing in CI before merge.

findings.title: Caching behavior tests were deleted without replacement
findings.body: The old test suite had a dedicated "Caching" describe block asserting that `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` return identical (cached) results on repeated calls. The refactor keeps the caching fields (`cachedAuthConditions`, `cachedFilterConditions`) and logic but the tests for it were removed entirely. Since the cache field types changed (from Prisma where-input objects to `Prisma.Sql`), a regression here (e.g., `Prisma.Sql` identity checks failing, or an always-truthy `1=0` fragment being treated as 'already computed') would go undetected.

findings.title: Final integration test asserts exact result set and depends on denormalized-table cleanup
findings.body: The `getBaseConditions` test runs `SELECT id FROM "BookingTimeStatusDenormalized" WHERE ${baseConditions}` and asserts the result is exactly one row (`[...toEqual([{ id: userBooking.id }])]`). Because `createTestData` also creates a booking tied to a team event type, and other tests/users may leave residual rows, any leftover denormalized row matching the same `userId`/`teamId IS NULL`/`eventTypeId` conditions will make this assertion fail or, conversely, hide bugs. The cleanup deletes the `Booking` rows but there is no explicit cleanup of `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized` rows; if that table is not cascade-deleted with bookings, stale rows from prior test runs will accumulate and break the strict `toEqual`. An assertion on membership (`results.some(r => r.id === userBooking.id)` / length filtering) or explicit denormalized-row cleanup would be more robust.
